raw_record.question_text:
In the transition-state structure shown in the image, calculate the total number of bonds in the structure, including single, double, and triple bonds but excluding those involving hydrogen.

Note: Disregard arrows. Consider all components present in the transition-state structure.

method.method_draft: First count the upper component. Count the upper-left MeO2C group as 4 heavy-atom bonds including its attachment to the alkene carbon; count the C=C alkene bond as 1; count the right ester attached to the alkene as 4 bonds including the alkene-C to carbonyl-C bond, C=O, C-O, and O-Me; count the alkene-C to S bond as 1; count the lower-left thioester side chain as S-CH2, CH2-C(=O), C=O, C-O, and O-Me = 5 bonds. This gives 15 for the upper component. Then count the lower-right thiolate ester component as S-CH2, CH2-C(=O), C=O, C-O, and O-Me = 5 bonds. Add both components: 15 + 5 = 20.

method.method_draft: Treat each ester/methoxycarbonyl group in the drawing as a standard R-C(=O)-O-Me fragment. There are four such ester units, and each contributes 4 heavy-atom bonds including its attachment to R, so they contribute 4 × 4 = 16 bonds. Next add heavy-atom bonds outside those ester fragments: the central alkene C=C bond = 1, the upper alkene carbon to sulfur bond = 1, the upper sulfur to CH2 bond = 1, and the lower thiolate sulfur to CH2 bond = 1. Total = 16 + 4 = 20.
